chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the pillow and the rug in which there are images/resemblances, so he said: 'There is no problem with it if it is in the house.' I said, 'The images/resembles?' He said: 'Everything that is trampled upon, so there is no problem with it.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to have images on pillows and rugs in a Muslim household?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) ruled that pillows and rugs featuring images (tathalith) are permissible for use in the house, provided they are frequently trampled upon (yutau'), as trampling diminishes their status as distinct images. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly principle that the prohibition of image-making primarily applies to objects of veneration or distinct display, whereas domestic items subjected to daily wear lose their 'image' status in a legal sense. The context of Chapter 65 in al-Kafi highlights the practical application of this distinction within household decor.
